payload.recommendation: spawn builder-agent to create math.js with intentional subtraction bug and a failing test
payload.reason: This workflow demonstrates SignalShape as a real inter-agent contract: a builder-agent emits a status after producing the buggy code, a debug-agent consumes the failing test output and emits a debug shape with the diagnosed root cause, and a fixer-agent consumes that debug message to apply the patch. Each handoff is a schema-validated JSON envelope rather than free-form prose, so the chain is machine-verifiable end-to-end. Seeding the repo with a known arithmetic bug (a - b instead of a + b) gives a deterministic failure that any downstream agent can reproduce, making the contract observable rather than hypothetical.

options_considered.option: ship math.js already correct and only simulate a debug exchange
options_considered.tradeoff: no real failing test, so the debug and fix shapes would carry fabricated payloads instead of evidence-backed ones

options_considered.option: use a heavy test runner like Jest or Vitest
options_considered.tradeoff: adds dependencies and install steps; node:test is built in and keeps the example reproducible with zero install

options_considered.option: introduce a more complex bug (e.g. floating point, async)
options_considered.tradeoff: obscures the contract demo behind domain complexity; a trivial off-by-operator bug keeps focus on the agent handoffs
